Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Diego CA
942 AM PST Wed Nov 18 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Cool weather will continue for the next week. Rain, isolated 
thunderstorms, high mountain snow, and stronger winds are 
expected Thursday into Thursday night as a storm system moves
through California. Dry but cool weather will follow Friday 
through Sunday. The next system looks weaker and could bring 
light rain Sunday night and Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO
COUNTIES...


...UPDATED AVIATION DISCUSSION...

Today will be fair but cool after the chilly start, with highs in
the mid 60s to lower 70s for lower elevations. That's about 4-10 
degrees below average for valleys, and about 1-3 degrees below 
average at the coast. The next storm Thursday will be pretty 
strong, with a well-defined front moving through SoCal. Rain 
should begin in the L.A. Basin Thursday morning, moving southeast 
into Riverside and San Diego Counties through the afternoon. Rain 
will be pretty intense along the front, and there is a small 
chance of thunderstorms. For both reasons, rainfall rates could 
reach 0.50-0.65 per hour, which could produce some urban flooding.
Snow levels will start out high, and drop to about 6,500 feet by 
the time the precipitation moves out. A few inches should 
accumulate above 7,500 feet, on the upper ski slopes around Big 
Bear. Down at Big Bear Lake, little if any accumulations are 
expected. But the timing of the cold air moving in with the 
moisture are uncertain, so there's a range of potential snowfall 
outcomes. Winds will be strongest ahead of and along the front, 
with gusts exceeding 25-30 mph for the coast and 40-55 mph in the 
mountains and adjacent desert slopes, where there's a wind 
advisory. Showers will follow the front Thursday evening as the 
snow level lowers, but then will eventually end Thursday night. 

Friday will start out quite cold, but clouds will clear to bring 
mostly sunny conditions. A secondary shortwave rotates through 
the Great Basin Friday, but for now it doesn't appear to prolong 
the precipitation, just postpone any warm up. A touch of offshore 
flow pays a visit Friday night and Saturday, but any brisk 
offshore winds will be quite isolated in foothills. High pressure 
aloft doesn't build much, but enough to provide dry and slightly 
warmer weather Friday through the weekend. Temperatures will 
continue below normal each of those days, with highs in the mid 
60s to lower 70s at lower elevations, upper 30s to mid 50s in the 
mountains, and 50s in the High Desert. Model guidance is starting 
to narrow the possibilities regarding the timing of the next 
precipitation. 

A weak shortwave moves into the region Sunday, bringing light 
showers Sunday night and Monday. Right now this system looks much 
weaker regarding precipitation amounts and winds. By Tuesday 
there's some guidance showing a continuation of the unsettled, 
occasionally wet and windy pattern. But there are nearly equal 
numbers of ensemble members showing a stronger ridge pattern for 
dry and warmer weather heading into the holiday.

&&

.AVIATION... 
181800Z...Coast/Valleys...SCT clouds with bases around 3000-4000 ft 
MSL, with intermittent low clouds going BKN this morning up to 20 
miles inland. Otherwise, SCT-BKN high clouds will build into the 
region into the afternoon and evening as a cold front approaches the 
area. BKN low clouds (2000-3000 ft MSL) increase and thicken going 
into the early morning hours Thursday. A band of rain will move 
through the region from north to south starting at KSNA around 16-
18Z down to KSAN closer to 19-21Z. This will bring areas of -RA and 
MVFR, locally IFR cigs/vis. Rain ending north to south Thursday 
afternoon / evening with slowly clearing cigs.

Mountains/Deserts...VFR conditions will prevail this morning. 
Building mid/high level clouds SCT-BKN AOA 15k feet MSL level clouds 
will build into the region after 00Z Thu. A band of rain will move 
through the region from north to south starting around 15-18Z in 
northern mountains, closer to 18-20Z in San Diego county. This will 
bring areas of -RA and MVFR, locally IFR cigs/vis. Rain ending north 
to south Thursday afternoon / evening with slowly clearing cigs.

&&

.MARINE...
A Small Craft Advisory has been issued for 12z Thursday through 18z 
Friday, as conditions look to deteriorate once again on Thursday as 
the next storm system approaches. Steep, high seas of 7-10 ft, along 
with wind gusts peaking 20-30 knots, are expected for Thursday into 
Friday morning. Wind direction initially south-southwest on Thursday 
will turn westerly by late afternoon and continue through early 
morning on Friday. Conditions will begin to improve by later in the 
day on Friday with much calmer seas expected by the weekend.

&&

.BEACHES...
The shorter period northwest swell will wane through this evening, 
leaving a 3-5 ft swell with a 13-14 second period for today. This 
will result in a brief decrease in surf, down to 3-5 feet. However, 
northwesterly swell builds again tomorrow, elevating surf once again 
by later in the evening and into early Friday.

Coastal flooding is expected at times through the rest of the week. 
King Tides are expected to peak next week, but chances of tides 
exceeding 7 ft start as early as Saturday Nov 21.

&&

.SKYWARN... 
Skywarn activation is not requested. However weather spotters are
encouraged to report significant weather conditions.

&&
